name: The Eagles Are Coming!
oracle_text:
Kicker {2}{W}{W} (You may pay an additional {2}{W}{W} as you cast this spell.)
Choose target creature you own. If this spell was kicked, instead choose any number of target creatures you own. Return each chosen creature to your hand. At the beginning of the next upkeep, create a 4/4 white Bird Soldier creature token with flying for each creature returned to your hand this way.
blocked_sentences: Choose target creature you own. If this spell was kicked, instead choose any number of target creatures you own. Return each chosen creature to your hand. At the beginning of the next upkeep, create a 4/4 white Bird Soldier creature token with flying for each creature returned to your hand this way.

needs.what: A target spec whose SIZE depends on a cost the caster paid -- "Choose target creature you own. If this spell was kicked, instead choose any number of target creatures you own." The size has to be settled at 601.2c, inside the cast, after kicker has been paid (601.2b/601.2f), which is exactly where `additional_paid` is already read for Marshal's Anthem's `count`. Suggested shape: let a target spec carry a `condition` from `condition_keys` alongside two sizes -- e.g. `{"id": "t1", "kind": "permanent", "count": 1, "count_if": {"condition": {"kicked": true}, "count": "any"}, "selector": {"zone": "battlefield", "types": ["Creature"], "owner": "you"}}` -- so that `enumerate_target_tuples` is offered one size on an unkicked cast and the variable-size enumeration on a kicked one. The plumbing exists on both sides: `kicked` is a live `condition_keys` entry read off the cast action, `count: "any"` is a supported variable size (Call the Coppercoats), and `TargetSpec.variable_size` (src/automtg/engine/carddef.py:111) already drives the storage split. What is missing is the switch between them at declaration time. This unblocks the whole "if this spell was kicked, instead choose any number of target ..." family (The Eagles Are Coming!, and the same template on Aether Gale's neighbours).
needs.why_existing_wont_do: `target_keys` is count/id/kind/mode/one_per_player/optional/selector/total_mana_value/up_to -- there is no `condition` on a target spec at all, so nothing in the language can ask whether the spell was kicked while targets are being declared. `count` as a value object is the nearest miss and cannot say it: `validate_value` (src/automtg/cards/loader/targets.py:303) accepts a number-valued expression such as `{"additional_paid": true}`, and "any number of" is not a number -- the loader spells it as the literal string `"any"` (src/automtg/cards/loader/targets.py:304, 219), which no value expression can evaluate to. Writing plain `count: "any"` drops the printed restriction and makes the unkicked mode strictly better than the card (bounce the whole board for {1}{W}); writing `count: 1` drops the kicker's entire payoff. Two specs is refused twice over: only one spec on a card may be variable-size (src/automtg/cards/loader/targets.py:133, "At most one spec may be variable-size"), and both specs would be declared on every cast anyway, so an unkicked cast could still pick many and a kicked one would be forced to pick an extra. The `mode` route is closed by name: a mode-owned target "must be a fixed number" (src/automtg/cards/loader/targets.py:193) and "a card-level variable-size target cannot share a card with a mode-owned one" (line 206) -- and `choose_mode`'s keys (all_if, budget, chooser, count, once_each, or_more, up_to, up_to_if) let the CASTER pick a mode, never a paid cost, so kicker could not force the second bullet either way. `kicker` itself is fully supported (`card_level_cost_keys`, and `{"kicked": true}` inside an `if` -- Into the Roil ships it), so this is not a kicker gap; it is the one thing kicker cannot yet change.

needs.what: An `as` binding on `return_to_hand`, recording the oids it actually moved, so a later effect can count them: "create a 4/4 ... token **for each creature returned to your hand this way**". With it the tail is one `delay` with `step: "upkeep"` whose `create_token` carries `amount: {"count": {"binding": "returned"}}` -- `op_delay` copies `ctx.bindings` into the DelayedTrigger at the moment it is created (src/automtg/engine/turn.py, `_run_delayed` rebuilds the context from `dict(delayed.bindings)`), and `{"binding": ...}` is already a `selector_keys` entry that `count` resolves (src/automtg/engine/effects/selectors.py:374). The change is three lines in `op_return_to_hand` (src/automtg/engine/effects/ops_cards.py:829) mirroring what `exile` and the ops at ops_cards.py:1072 and :1927 already do -- bind the list of oids that were moved, not the ones that were asked for -- plus `as` in its `op_options`.
needs.why_existing_wont_do: `return_to_hand`'s whole spec is `objects` (packet `op_options`, and src/automtg/engine/effects/ops_cards.py:829-838 reads nothing else), so the set it moved is discarded the instant it resolves. `{"target": "t1"}` inside the delay is refused by name -- `_refuse_targets_inside_a_delay` (src/automtg/cards/loader/effects.py:235) raises because `turn._run_delayed` builds the delayed context with `targets={}` (603.7: the delayed trigger does not inherit the creating ability's targets) -- and that refusal's own docstring names this exact idiom as the fix: "`as` on the op that moved the card, and `binding` on the op that brings it back". `snapshot` is the other near miss and is the wrong shape twice: it captures `oids[0]` only (src/automtg/engine/effects/ops_control.py:740-756), so it cannot hold the "any number" a kicked cast returns, and it binds a characteristics dict rather than a list of oids, which `count` cannot count. No `value_keys` entry reads it either -- `cards_from_graveyard_this_turn`, `permanents_entered_this_turn` and `creatures_died_this_turn` are the turn ledgers that exist, and none of them counts cards returned to a hand, let alone "this way". Wrapping the whole tail in a `for_each` over the targets and scheduling one single-token `delay` per creature is the only shape that loads today, and it is a different card written down: it installs N delayed triggered abilities where the printing has one, so it fires N separate times at that upkeep and reads wrongly to anything that counts triggers or batches token creation.

notes: The Kicker line itself is NOT blocked and needs no work: `kicker` is a `card_level_cost_keys` entry and the card would simply carry "kicker": "{2}{W}{W}" (Into the Roil ships exactly that), with `{"kicked": true}` available as an `if` condition. Only the second paragraph is blocked, on three independent counts. The cheapest of the three by far is the token -- a one-line addition to data/cards/tokens.cards.json -- but closing it alone leaves the card unwritable: the kicked target count has no spelling at all, and without an `as` on `return_to_hand` the delayed trigger has no honest way to learn how many creatures it returned. All three must land before this card can be authored.
